source.title: Neural Characteristic Activation Analysis and Geometric Parameterization for ReLU Networks

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including appendices; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: The paper varies batch size under a fixed 90-epoch schedule and reports validation accuracy, testing the batch-size portion of V5 with a different training setup.
record.gate_note: The ImageNet32 VGG-6 experiment tests V5. Other reported results compare parameterizations or measure activation-boundary stability and generalization, but do not test another listed version. Cited results are not extracted.
record.test_reason: Table 2 tests V5 in a new setting: VGG-6 on ImageNet32, varying batch size across six parameterizations while holding training to 90 epochs. Within-parameterization batch comparisons measure the claimed held-out performance penalty.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the authors' conclusion: they argue that GmP resolves an activation-boundary instability and improves stability, convergence speed, and generalization in their evaluations. They report GmP+IMN as best on ImageNet32 at each tested batch size and describe its relative advantage as increasing with batch size. This does not mean its own accuracy increases monotonically with batch size.
record.recipe_differences: The paper proposes a hyperspherical weight parameterization and evaluates it against standard, weight, and batch normalization. Its ImageNet32 batch-size comparison uses 90 epochs and learning rates selected by cross-validation; it does not reproduce a cited large-batch study's recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: On ImageNet32, validation accuracy varies with batch size and parameterization. The authors report learning rates selected by cross-validation and an improvement from adding IMN to GmP.

fits_no_version.finding: Theoretical and illustrative results show smaller changes in characteristic activation boundaries under GmP; separate benchmark comparisons report improved held-out performance.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Geometric parameterization stabilizes ReLU activation-boundary evolution and can improve optimization and held-out performance.

record.peer_reviewed: NeurIPS 2024 (the supplied metadata says Neural Information Processing Systems, 2023; the paper text states 38th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2024)).
record.problems: The batch-size evidence is from one architecture and one dataset, and reports validation accuracy rather than train-test error gaps. Batch sizes are compared under the paper's selected learning rates; the study does not isolate a general batch-size effect across recipes.
record.rows_left_out: No eligible results omitted. The paper's other parameterization comparisons and test metrics do not measure one of the listed claim versions.

untested.parts: No fixed random-label fitting or corresponding held-out comparison.
No width sweep or identification of the width needed for zero training error.
No controlled convolutional versus fully connected image-classification comparison.
No reported adaptive-optimizer versus SGD comparison; the setup's preference for SGD is attributed to prior work.

No language models, longer-training remedy, learning-rate scaling or warmup intervention, or systematic batch-threshold estimate. Batch-size results cover only VGG-6 on ImageNet32 at 90 epochs; normalization and parameterization choices are compared.
No magnitude-scaled weight-perturbation sharpness measure, generalization-gap ranking, or comparison with norm and margin measures.
No memorization-based example removal and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: All 36 table values match the supplied text. Within-parameterization batch comparisons are eligible evidence even though the paper introduces GmP. Learning rates were selected by cross-validation, with 0.1 reported for GmP and 0.01 for other methods on ImageNet32; batch-specific tuning details and the meaning of the reported ± values are not specified. Improvements at selected larger batches qualify scope rather than challenge V5's workload-dependent threshold and recipe exceptions. No additional eligible result is missing beyond the record's declared exclusions.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label training or natural-label versus random-label held-out comparison.
No width sweep beyond the interpolation threshold.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison.
No adaptive optimizer versus SGD held-out comparison; optimizer references in setup are not comparative results.

The experiment tests VGG-6 on ImageNet32 over batch sizes 256, 512, and 1024 for a fixed 90 epochs. It does not test language models, other architectures, or longer training and recipe adaptations as remedies.
No magnitude-aware sharpness or comparison of generalization-gap measures.
No removal of memorized training examples.

relationships.condition: VGG-6 on ImageNet32, 90 epochs, SP, WN, WN+MBN, or BN; batches 512 and 1024 versus 256.
relationships.reason: R14–R18, R20–R24, R26–R30, and R32–R36 show declining top-1 and top-5 accuracy; top-1 losses at batch 1024 range from 1.40 to 3.29 percentage points.
relationships.display_finding: The study reports lower top-1 and top-5 accuracy across the compared parameterizations, but these comparisons remain unverified.

relationships.condition: VGG-6 on ImageNet32, 90 epochs, GmP+IMN; batch 1024 versus 256.
relationships.reason: R3 and R6 show top-1 and top-5 accuracy falling from 43.14% and 67.36% to 42.70% and 66.98%.
relationships.display_finding: The study reports small declines in top-1 and top-5 accuracy with GmP+IMN, but these comparisons remain unverified.

relationships.condition: VGG-6 on ImageNet32, 90 epochs, GmP+IMN; batch 512 versus 256.
relationships.reason: R2 and R5 improve by 0.48 and 0.40 percentage points, showing that the penalty does not begin at batch 512 under this recipe.
relationships.display_finding: Accuracy improvements of 0.48 and 0.40 percentage points were reported, but these batch comparisons remain unverified.

relationships.condition: VGG-6 on ImageNet32, 90 epochs, GmP; batches 512 and 1024 versus 256.
relationships.reason: R8–R12 show both larger batches outperforming 256 on both metrics, although 1024 underperforms 512; the batch-size response depends on parameterization and the comparison interval.
relationships.display_finding: Both larger batches reportedly outperformed batch 256 while batch 1024 underperformed 512, but these comparisons remain unverified.
